claims.text: Current large language models are insufficient for accurate probabilistic estimations.
Large language models can generate relevant factors that affect probabilities.
Large language models can produce coarse-grained probabilities when given more complete information.
Large language models can help determine which factors are relevant to specific downstream contexts.
BIRD aligns a Bayesian network with LLM abductions to estimate probabilities in a deduction step.
BIRD provides probability estimations that are 30% better than direct LLM baselines.

evidence.description: Current large language models (LLMs) are insufficient for accurate estimations
they can generate relevant factors that may affect the probabilities
produce coarse-grained probabilities when the information is more complete
help determine which factors are relevant to specific downstream contexts
We propose BIRD, a novel probabilistic inference framework that aligns a Bayesian network with LLM abductions and then estimates more accurate probabilities in a deduction step.
We show BIRD provides reliable probability estimations that are 30% better than those provided directly by LLM baselines.
